fixers.name: Ernesto Sandoval
dialogue: Welcome to New Detroit. You look like a man who's hungry for work.
Depends on the work. And the man offering it.
Sandoval. Ernesto Sandoval. I deal in acquisitions.
That's a word people use when the real one sounds worse.
It's a word that keeps a man out of court. Sit down, Captain.
I'll stand. What's the run?
Forty units of iron. Here to the Liverpool refinery, over in Newcastle.
Iron. That's it.
Strictly legit. No contraband, no hassles. Just a short jump from here.
If it's that clean, why are you buying me a drink instead of posting it?
Because the posted board is full of men who ask fewer questions and lose more cargo. I'd rather pay for judgment.
Flattery's cheap. What's the pay?
Fifteen thousand credits on your return.
On my return.
I don't have it on me tonight.
Then we don't have a deal tonight.
Wait. I'll show you something better than credits.
Here. Hold this. Collateral, until I pay.
What is it?
Don't ask me what it is.
It's warm.
Just keep it safe. And keep it quiet -- inside your jacket, not on your console.
You're handing a stranger something you won't name, and telling him to hide it. You see how that sounds.
I see how it sounds. Bring it back with you and there's another five thousand in it for you.
Twenty total, then. For hauling iron.
For hauling iron, and for having a short memory.
Deliver at Liverpool. My people will meet the ship. Then come back here.
And if you're not here when I get back?
I'll be here.
fixers.offer: Haul 40 units of iron to Liverpool (Newcastle system), then return here for 15,000 credits - plus 5,000 for returning his collateral. Deal?

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: I'm looking for Sandoval.
Don't bother. He's dead.
Two nights ago. Word is it wasn't an accident.
He owed me fifteen thousand credits.
He owed a lot of people a lot of things. You're near the back of that line.
Who are you?
Tayla. I keep track of who's breathing in this sector. It's a growth industry lately.
And you tracked me down why?
Because Sandoval handed you a trinket before he died, and now the people he owed are very curious about where it went.
It's collateral. It's his.
It's yours. He's in no position to redeem it, and his fifteen grand died with him. Keep it, like it or not.
I'd rather hand it back and walk away clean.
Hand it back to who? There's no one left to hand it to -- that's the point. You're holding it now. That's the whole story.
Then tell me what I'm holding.
I'll tell you this much for free. Sandoval didn't buy that thing.
He got it by killing the man who owned it.
You're telling me I'm carrying a murder motive.
I'm telling you death follows it, $CS. Feel lucky?
Not particularly.
Good. Lucky men die out here first.
You know more than you're saying.
Of course I do. That's the only thing I sell.
What's the price?
You fly for me. I'll trade the rest out a piece at a time, and you'll earn every piece.
That's a long way of saying you own me.
It's a long way of saying you're the only one who can carry that thing without being searched. Come see me when you're ready to work.

dialogue: Ready to work? Good. First job's a milk run.
Nothing about the last week has been a milk run.
Thirty units of plastics. Completely legal, nothing to hide.
Then why are you smiling?
Because officially you're running it to Newcastle.
And actually?
Actually you'll divert to Oakham. Hidden pirate base out in Pentonville.
A falsified manifest. That's a jump up from hauling iron.
The paperwork is for anyone watching. The cargo really is plastics -- if they board you, you're clean.
And if they check the flight recorder?
Then you're a pilot who got lost. It happens.
Oakham sits in an asteroid field. Mind your speed on approach -- I've lost two people to rocks and none to guns.
The pirates don't shoot?
While you fly for me, Pentonville's pirates keep their guns to themselves. That's what you're really buying.
Ten thousand?
Ten thousand on delivery. Leave the ship docked and meet me in the Oakham bar. We'll talk more there.
More about the artifact.
More about whatever you've earned by then.

dialogue: Now the real work.
The milk run's over, then.
Brilliance. Yes -- that Brilliance. To Hector, the mining base in Troy.
That's not a manifest problem. That's a prison sentence.
Fifteen units. It'll fit where nobody looks.
Troy's crawling with militia.
It is. Talons, and they scan everything that moves.
You're sending me through a checkpoint with contraband in the hold.
I'm sending you through it fast. Do not stop. Do not fight. Burn past them and dock.
And if they light me up?
Then you run, and you don't lead them back here.
Charming.
Fifteen thousand on delivery at Hector. Then get yourself back here in one piece.
And another piece of the story.
You're learning.

Should I be watching my back?

Here's the rest of what I owe you, first.
Before Sandoval, it belonged to a spice merchant named Deiter.
And before him?
Deiter had it from his own father. Every owner I can name died holding it.
That's a pattern, not a story.
That's where my thread runs out. I've sent the holo on to someone who can actually read it.
Who?
Roman Lynch. New Constantinople. A thug -- but an expert on exotic and valuable things.
A thug.

fixers.name: Roman Lynch
dialogue: You don't wanna talk to me, 'cause I don't wanna talk to you.
I'm here to see Lynch.
Mr. Lynch, sittin' over there, HE'S the one you wanna talk to. So state your bidness or take a hike, buddy.
Enough, Miggs.
Ah, Captain. I've been expecting you. I am Roman Lynch.
Tayla said you'd see me.
You may speak freely around my assistant. He is exceedingly loyal.
He's exceedingly something.
Your artifact interests me, $NM.
Everyone finds it interesting. Nobody will tell me what it is.
There is a hologram inside it. Did you know?
A hologram. And you'd know that how?
Because Tayla sent me an image, and my people are thorough. It is a map, or something that behaves like one.
A map to what?
That is precisely the question I intend to answer -- while you make yourself useful.
There it is.
A certain Captain Seelig is loitering at Nav 3 in Pentonville. His ship is the Hooded Hawk.
And?
Deliver a message. Tell him how profoundly disappointed I am in him. Verbatim, please.
That's all. Words.
Words, Captain. I am a businessman.
Businessmen don't need couriers for a comm channel.
Some messages lose their meaning over a relay. Ten thousand when you get back.
And the artifact?
Stays with you. I want it studied, not stolen -- and frankly it is safer in a ship than in my safe.
A simple courier run.
What could go wrong?

You used me as a trigger, Lynch.
I used you as a messenger. What he did with the message was his choice.
Your ten thousand, as agreed.

People keep dying around it. Fascinating, really.

My analysts refused to write a number down. That knowledge cost me three of them.
Cost them what?
Their positions, Captain. What did you think I meant?
Before we discuss it further, I need a favor.
Of course you do.
My cousin Regis has been subpoenaed in a murder trial.

A tedious man's. It would be best for everyone if Regis simply disappeared before he testifies.
You want me to disappear a witness.
I want you to give a relative a ride. The distinction matters to lawyers, so it should matter to you.

fixers.name: Masterson
dialogue: I need access to the Oxford archive.
Ah. The pilot with the artifact and the trail of dead mobsters.
News travels.
Masterson. University administration. And no -- the library is CLOSED to you.
I can pay.
Everyone can pay. That is what makes payment uninteresting.
Then what's interesting?
Service. The university needs work done, and I am nothing if not transactional.
How much work?
Access is an endowment, paid in four installments. Complete them and I unlock the archive myself.
Four favors for a library card. That's quite a fee.
It is quite a library.
First installment. Hunter Toth is inbound in a Drayman at the Saxtogue jump point.
Who is he?
A journalist. He wrote unkind truths about the Retros, and Retros hold grudges with unusual sincerity.
So they'll be waiting for him.
Meet him there and see him to the planet. He must be ON THE GROUND before you land.
Before I land.
I will not pay for a corpse with an honor guard. Ten thousand, and one installment struck from your debt.

fixers.name: Oxford Library
dialogue: The archive terminal accepts Masterson's authorization.
You place the artifact in the scanner cradle. The cradle hums.
MATCH FOUND. Classification: STELTEK.
A precursor civilization. Starfaring while humanity was learning fire.
No verified contact in recorded history. No recovered vessels. No remains.
The artifact is a power relay of unknown function.
Energy signature: dormant, but not dead.
Cross-reference: recent anomalous Steltek-band readings reported near PALAN.
Appended note. Dr. Monkhouse, the sector's leading xenoarchaeologist, has been asking the same questions you are.
Last known location: the Palan system.

fixers.name: Lynn Murphy
dialogue: You tried to land on Palan, didn't you?
I got as far as the orbital line.
Bounty hunters have the planet sewn up tight. The name's Murphy -- only my close friends call me Lynn.
Understood.
Two corporations here. Rondell and Bronte.
And the hunters?
Bronte hired them. Choke off Rondell's food exports, ship their own in to fill the gap, take the market.
People are starving so a corporation can move a decimal point.
Now you understand Palan.
And you're what, the resistance?
I run it for Rondell out of this refinery. Hired resistance -- I won't pretend otherwise.
At least you're honest about it.
Honesty's free. Everything else out here costs.
So what do you need?
The blockade rotates fresh ships through the asteroid field. Cut the reinforcements and the whole thing starves.
How many?
Three waves of Demons. Kill every last one and come back.
And the pay?
Fifteen thousand. Most of what we have -- so try to be worth it.

fixers.name: Dr. Lemuel Monkhouse
dialogue: Doctor Monkhouse?
Don't speak to me about extraterrestrial artifacts. I'm sick of them!
I haven't said a word about one.
You have the look. I nearly got killed on this rock because of my work.
Lemuel Monkhouse. Xenoarchaeology. Formerly of several institutions that no longer return my calls.
How did you end up on Palan?
I didn't COME to Palan, young man. I was brought.
Brought.
Kidnapped. By men who wanted my Steltek fragment.
Kidnapped. And they're still looking for you?
They are buried under their own interrogation compound. The bombing had one merciful outcome.
You may take a moment. Everyone does.
You said fragment. You have a piece of one.
Thirty years I've given the Steltek. Show me your piece and I'll tell you what it is.
Here.
Oh. Oh, my.
Doctor?
My instruments are at the Basra refinery, and I detest cramped quarters. Fly me there.
That's it? A lift?
Five thousand credits toward your expenses, and every answer I have.
Then why do you look nervous?
Because someone else has been asking about me. Someone with FUR.
Fur. You're saying Kilrathi.
I am saying we should leave promptly.

My fragment -- look. Look here. It FITS yours.

Why split it?
